The people who report here are second-hand holders, not the original investors: \"In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant\", and such buyers \"are not able to claim a deduction for the costs of acquiring the forestry interest\" and instead carry them in the cost base. The gain arises on sale of the interest or on receipt of harvest proceeds.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2022/part-a-about-capital-gains-tax/forestry-managed-investment-scheme-interests","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Forestry managed investment scheme interest: Capital gains - discount method","k":"Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Thinning receipts are also excluded, being assessable income rather than capital proceeds.","where":["pmp-cgt-2000-01 / cgt_2000_01","pmp-cgt-2001-02 / cgt_2001_02","pmp-cgt-2002-03 / cgt_2002_03","pmp-cgt-2003-04 / cgt_2003_04","pmp-cgt-2004-05 / cgt_2004_05","pmp-cgt-2005-06 / cgt_2005_06","pmp-cgt-2006-07 / cgt_2006_07","pmp-cgt-2007-08 / cgt_2007_08","pmp-cgt-2008-09 / cgt_2008_09","pmp-cgt-2009-10 / cgt_2009_10","pmp-cgt-2010-11 / cgt_2010_11","pmp-cgt-2011-12 / cgt_2011_12","and 1 more"]},{"n":"N_ACTV_FMIS_INDX_Y","d":"Gains on a forestry scheme interest worked out under indexation, a box that in practice is almost never used.","full":"Gains on a forestry scheme interest worked out under indexation, a box that in practice is almost never used. The ATO treats a forestry interest as a CGT asset only for a later buyer: \"You are a subsequent participant if you are not an initial participant\", and \"Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes\". Indexation needs an acquisition before 21 September 1999, which is years before the forestry scheme rules and this row existed.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2022/part-a-about-capital-gains-tax/forestry-managed-investment-scheme-interests","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Forestry managed investment scheme interest: Capital gains - indexation method","k":"Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The ATO treats such an interest as a CGT asset only where it is not trading stock: \"If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest.\" The gain here is simply proceeds less cost base.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2022/part-a-about-capital-gains-tax/forestry-managed-investment-scheme-interests","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Forestry managed investment scheme interest: Other capital gains","k":"Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no method-based reduction to come. The taxation of financial arrangements rules do this deliberately: they allow \"gains and losses from certain hedging financial arrangements to be characterised and taxed in accordance with the tax treatment of the underlying item being hedged\". Where the hedged item is a CGT asset, the ATO instructs the entity to \"specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule\".","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2016/introduction/cgt-and-the-tofa-rules/hedging-financial-arrangements","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Hedging financial arrangements: Capital gains - discount method","k":"Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The ATO explains that under a valid election \"gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged\". The old schedule gives the hedging row only these two boxes, discount and other; there is no indexation box.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2016/introduction/cgt-and-the-tofa-rules/hedging-financial-arrangements","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Hedging financial arrangements: Other capital gains","k":"Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no later method-based reduction. This is the largest and least specific of the non-active rows, and the one most likely to move when the form is redesigned.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Other CGT assets and any other CGT events: Capital gains - discount method","k":"Other CGT assets and events, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Indexation confines it further to assets acquired before 11:45 am on 21 September 1999.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Other CGT assets and any other CGT events: Capital gains - indexation method","k":"Other CGT assets and events, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, measured against an indexed cost base. For a company this is where most non-real-estate, non-share gains end up, because a company cannot use the discount column beside it.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Other CGT assets and any other CGT events: Other capital gains","k":"Other CGT assets and events, other method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no further method-based reduction. This is the cell where an investment property sale by a trust or a superannuation fund normally lands.","dsrc":"ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-schedule-2024-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-cgt-schedule-and-tax-return-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Real estate: Capital gains - discount method","k":"Real estate capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses. The ATO explains that the method \"allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999)\", and that \"The indexation of the cost base of an asset is frozen on 30 September 1999.\" Because indexation stops there, a long-held property indexed in 2010 gets no relief for the eleven years since.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Indexation method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Real estate: Capital gains - indexation method","k":"Real estate capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The ATO puts the calculation plainly: \"To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.\" Against the discount cell on the same row, a large figure here points to quick turnover or to a company vendor.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Real estate: Other capital gains","k":"Real estate capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, and with no later reduction on the discount side of the form. The ATO reserves the discount method for \"assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method\", and adds that \"the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies\". The amount is the whole gain, not the halved one, because the discount is applied later at part F.","dsrc":"ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-schedule-2024-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-cgt-schedule-and-tax-return-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Shares and units (in unit trusts): Capital gains - discount method","k":"Shares and units capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Non-active is the residual side of the grid: \"If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets\".","dsrc":"ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method and Step 2 active assets","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-schedule-2024-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-cgt-schedule-and-tax-return-2024","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Shares and units (in unit trusts): Capital gains - indexation method","k":"Shares and units capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. A gain on shares bought after September 1999 has to be reported in the discount or other column instead, so this cell tracks the age of the holding as much as the asset class. The old schedule also runs shares and units together and does not separate listed from unlisted, so it cannot measure exposure to the Australian market.","where":["pmp-cgt-2000-01 / cgt_2000_01","pmp-cgt-2001-02 / cgt_2001_02","pmp-cgt-2002-03 / cgt_2002_03","pmp-cgt-2003-04 / cgt_2003_04","pmp-cgt-2004-05 / cgt_2004_05","pmp-cgt-2005-06 / cgt_2005_06","pmp-cgt-2006-07 / cgt_2006_07","pmp-cgt-2007-08 / cgt_2007_08","pmp-cgt-2008-09 / cgt_2008_09","pmp-cgt-2009-10 / cgt_2009_10","pmp-cgt-2010-11 / cgt_2010_11","pmp-cgt-2011-12 / cgt_2011_12","and 1 more"]},{"n":"N_ACTV_SHARES_UNITS_OTH_C","d":"Capital gains on shares and units that get neither indexation nor the discount, which in practice means parcels bought and sold inside twelve months.","full":"Capital gains on shares and units that get neither indexation nor the discount, which in practice means parcels bought and sold inside twelve months. The ATO defines the calculation as follows: \"To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.\" Read against the discount cell on the same row, this column is a rough marker of short-held trading rather than long-term holding.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/guide-to-capital-gains-tax-2025/appendixes/appendix-4-definitions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-active assets - Shares and units (in unit trusts): Other capital gains","k":"Shares and units capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The ATO puts the question as \"At the end of the income year, did the company still have any assets that were acquired before 20 September 1985 and that were not treated as post-CGT assets under Division 149?\" Division 149 resets the cost base of a pre-1985 asset once the majority underlying ownership of the company changes, so a yes marks a company still carrying genuinely grandfathered assets. The ATO's instruction is short - \"Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement\" - but the surrounding rule is what matters: a seller completes labels D and E only \"for arrangements which don't involve look-through earnout rights\". ABS keeps the joining information away from the data itself: the \"Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data\". Read this column with ENTITY_TYPE and BN on the same row, because a CGT schedule is lodged by a taxpaying entity, and a person-level count of gains that ignores the entity type will mix individuals with the companies, trusts and funds beside them.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic MADIP Person ID","k":"PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)","def":"An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, stable across every column of the row and across the twenty-four year tables. The ATO says a taxpayer uses one of three methods for each asset - \"indexation method\", \"discount method, or\" the \"'other' method\" - and the discount method is available only where the asset was held at least twelve months: \"If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method\". The split matters because the discount is not applied yet: \"If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years.\"","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax","durl":"https://caat-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/62327127-22dc-4be1-8fbe-031cb313496a_7bbe17ea_9cd6_4c09_8d67_211d38ed98e8_pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total current year capital gains (CYCG) - Capital gains - discount method","k":"Capital gains amount, discount method (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. The ATO limits it to a CGT event on \"an asset you acquired before 11.45am on 21 September 1999\" that was held for twelve months or more, and the indexation itself stops early: \"As indexation is frozen as at 30 September 1999, you can index your cost base only up to the September 1999 quarter.\" Read against the discount-method and other-method totals on the same row, this column marks the disposal of assets held since the old regime.","dsrc":"ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), the indexation method","durl":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=4151-5.2001","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total current year capital gains (CYCG) - Capital gains - indexation method","k":"Capital gains amount, indexation method (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions. It is the only date on the row: the income year the figures belong to is carried by INCM_YR, and no column records when a CGT event actually happened. Its practical use is vintage, telling you how long after the end of an income year a record was settled, and how far apart two rows for the same year were processed.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Processed date","k":"ATO processing date","def":"A calendar date.
